request: Bei welchen Haendlern ist mein Durchschnittsbon am hoechsten? Nur die, wo ich mindestens fuenfmal war.

plan.title: Hoechster Durchschnittsbon je Haendler
plan.question: Ausgaben je Haendler 2025 geteilt durch die Zahl der Buchungen bei diesem Haendler, nur Haendler mit mindestens fuenf Buchungen, die acht groessten Durchschnitte, eine Zeile je Haendler, Spalten merchant und avg_eur.

sql:
SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS merchant,
       ROUND(-SUM(amount) / COUNT(*), 2) AS avg_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0 AND category IN ('Supermarket', 'Bakery')
GROUP BY merchant
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY avg_eur DESC
LIMIT 8
reasoning_plan:
the request is German, so language de
eine Rangfolge ueber Haendlernamen, die lang werden
liegende Balken tragen lange Namen
the columns are merchant, avg_eur, the euro figure last
der Zeitraum ist das ganze Jahr 2025
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar_horizontal, so the mark is barX and nothing else
the columns are merchant and avg_eur, and avg_eur holds the numbers
barX draws sideways, so the euro column is x and the names are y
scales.x is the euro axis and scales.y the band of names, none dropped

request: Zeig pro Monat den Tagesschnitt unserer Ausgaben, aufgeteilt nach Kategorie.

plan.title: Tagesschnitt je Monat nach Kategorie
plan.question: Ausgaben jedes Monats 2025 je Kategorie geteilt durch die Zahl der Tage dieses Monats, eine Zeile je Monat und Kategorie, nie zwei Zeilen fuer dasselbe Paar, jede Kategorie unter ihrem eigenen Namen, Spalten month als 'YYYY-MM', topic und per_day_eur.

sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month,
       CASE WHEN lower(description) LIKE '%edeka%' THEN 'Supermarkt'
            WHEN lower(description) LIKE '%aral%' THEN 'Tanken'
            ELSE 'Rest' END AS topic,
       ROUND(-SUM(amount) / 30.0, 2) AS per_day_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0
GROUP BY month, topic
ORDER BY month, topic

Monate und Kategorien kreuzen sich, und der ganze Tagessatz zaehlt
gestapelte Balken addieren die Kategorien zum Tagessatz
the columns are month, topic, per_day_eur, the euro figure last
der Zeitraum ist das ganze Jahr 2025
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar_stacked, so barY carries a series and no layout
the columns are month, topic and per_day_eur, and per_day_eur holds the numbers
topic is the series, so it is the z and the color channel and it needs a legend
a stack is taller than any single row, so the euro axis names no domain

request: Show me how my spending piled up day by day in November.

plan.title: Spending piling up in November
plan.question: Spending of November 2025 added up day by day, one row per day with a booking, the running total, columns day as 'YYYY-MM-DD' and cumulative_eur.

sql:
WITH per_day AS (
  SELECT booked_on AS day, -SUM(amount) AS spent
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0 AND booked_on >= '2024-11-01' AND booked_on < '2024-12-01'
  GROUP BY day
)
SELECT day,
       ROUND(SUM(spent) OVER (ORDER BY day), 2) AS cumulative_eur
FROM per_day
ORDER BY day
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
'piled up' is a running total over the days of one month
an area shows how fast it grows
the columns are day, cumulative_eur, the euro figure last
the period is November 2025, the month before the newest booking
reasoning_code:
the shape is area, so areaY draws the band and lineY its edge
the columns are day and cumulative_eur, and cumulative_eur holds the numbers
the days read as periods (2025-11-04), so the axis formats them with monthShort and may thin the labels
an area rests on zero, so its euro axis is the bare scaleLinear factory
